_readme: Creator Marketing and Partnerships, Version 1.3: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/creator-campaigns.astro and src/components/creator/). Version 1.3 is John's delta brief (October 2026) against the deployed Version 1.2: the creator network is gone, with nothing in its place, so the program context (which gains one quieter line on the roster) leads straight into the campaign atlas, and the eight creators and their affiliations appear only in the credits; the Singapore loop is rebuilt around the party-bus game show, high tea on the 56th floor and the city, with one shopping moment and no retail signage; the Mykonos loop gains the aftermovie's Lock In Podcast production moment; the Trezor Dare Ad's performance highlights take the centered, display-scale composition of the Technical Product Marketing results and its quotation's four phrases are set apart by type alone; the ownership wave flows again; the selected-content library gains Podcasts (seven formats) and its creator ads trade Jungle Talk for a Trezor Dare Ad excerpt, and a format the reader selects loops until they select another or leave the section. Everything else is Version 1.2 (and before it Version 1.1: the approved copy and the confirmed roster and affiliations). Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json; every slot already holds its final aspect ratio, all of them square or landscape.

hero._hero: 05 Hero: one full-screen landscape composition in layers (the coastal-estate reference, used for the hero only): the sky, the headline, the villa and its palms in front of the headline's lower line, and two palm fronds at the corners, each moving at its own rate as the page scrolls, with a slow drift of their own; reduced motion holds the layers still. The photographs are illustrative stock (Unsplash), credited once, in the credits (V1.1), and never presented as footage from the trips. V1.2: the paragraph names John's ownership only; the collaborators are credited in the credits.
hero.label: 01 / Creator Marketing and Partnerships
hero.headline: Creator campaigns, built to travel.
hero.copy: I helped lead creator programs across Costa Rica, Singapore, and Mykonos, owning campaign strategy, creative direction, sponsor coordination, on-site production, and distribution.

context._context: 06 Program context (V1.3): no kicker; John's headline, its closing phrase in the accent, and one paragraph on what he led and helped plan, naming no collaborators (they are credited in the credits); beneath it `roster`, one smaller, quieter line on the eight creators and the fields they came from (V1.3: no names, handles, pictures, follower counts, categories or travel histories). No services grid and no list of roles. The creator network that followed it is gone (V1.3), so the context leads straight into the atlas.
context.headline: Each destination became a campaign in motion.
context.copy: For Bolt Liquidity, each trip brought creators, sponsors, and a production plan together for a few focused days. I led campaign strategy with co-sponsors, sponsor coordination, creative direction, on-site shoot planning, approvals, distribution, and reporting, and helped plan the travel, logistics, and production that made each activation possible.
context.roster: The roster brought together eight creators across streaming, crypto media, ecosystem leadership, entertainment, and community.

atlas._atlas: 09 Campaign atlas: one stage that holds still while the reader scrolls through three states, Costa Rica, Singapore and Mykonos, each with its own loop (5 to 10 seconds, silent, landscape, reset with a dissolve), two fragments, color atmosphere, large name, chapter index and concise copy. Wide screens with motion allowed pin it; narrow or short screens, reduced motion and no JavaScript show the three chapters one after another. Counts: creators as the V1.0 roster counted them (6, 7 and 4), content pieces as John gave them in V1.1 (40+, 35+ and 25+). `sponsors` names logo ids in src/data/logos.json. V1.2: no visible kicker; `heading` names the section for assistive technology only (the unused V1.0 `title` is gone). V1.3: the Singapore loop is rebuilt around the city, the party-bus game show and high tea on the 56th floor (the girls photographing the food, its details, the creators at the table) with one shopping moment and no retail signage, and the Mykonos loop gains the aftermovie's Lock In Podcast production moment between the water and the villa; Costa Rica is unchanged.
atlas.heading: Campaign atlas

destinations.name: Costa Rica
destinations.copy: A creator house on the Pacific coast where shared moments became destination content, creator-led integrations, and bespoke campaigns produced for co-sponsors.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.copy: A crypto game show on a party bus, high tea on the 56th floor, and a shopping spree through the city's luxury malls, designed as a conference activation.

destinations.name: Mykonos
destinations.copy: A villa above the Aegean, a day on a catamaran, and long dinners into the evening, with four creators turning each moment into content.

trezor._trezor: 10 Trezor Dare Ad (V1.3): the final video first (Trezor Dare Ad.mp4, with sound, on request), then the assignment, the objective and the approach (John's words), three performance highlights from the creator's own account (compared with that account's preceding three months, never presented as Trezor's total campaign performance; the third is #2 by reach, never most-viewed), set since V1.3 in the centered, display-scale composition of the Technical Product Marketing results (a centered label, one row of three, the percentile and `metricsNote` as quieter lines under it), and Trezor's feedback (the approved quotation, one continuous quote whose four phrases, listed in `emphasis` and each found once in the quotation, are set apart by type alone since V1.3: the deep teal and a slightly heavier weight, no marker). No collaboration block: the credits at the foot of the page keep that record.
trezor.title: Trezor Dare Ad
trezor.deck: A creator-led sponsor integration for Trezor, filmed at the creator house in Costa Rica.

brief.label: Assignment
brief.text: Create a creator-led campaign that places Trezor's new device inside a culturally relevant, community-driven moment rather than a conventional product demonstration.

brief.label: Objective
brief.text: Build affinity with crypto culture and community while highlighting the device's Bluetooth connectivity and refined, modern design.

brief.label: Approach
brief.text: Turn the product into the center of a playful dare filmed with creators at the Costa Rica house, using a real social setting to demonstrate wireless use, showcase the device's design, and make the integration feel native rather than ad-like.

trezor.metricsNote: Measured on the creator's own account against that account's preceding three months. These are creator-account results, not Trezor's total campaign performance.

library._library: 11 Selected content (V1.3): a library of seven edits from across the three trips, one per format, each a curated mini-edit of its own (silent, landscape, 7 to 14 seconds) whose last moment dissolves back into its own opening, so it can repeat with no seam; chosen with simple text tabs and a restrained active line that fills as the edit plays. Until the reader chooses, with motion allowed, the library moves on to the next format as each edit ends, round and round (holding while keyboard focus is in the formats); a format the reader selects is pinned: its edit plays from the start and loops until they select another or leave the section (V1.3), after which the library moves on again. The reader can pause at any time; it pauses off screen and in a hidden tab. Reduced motion, a data-saving preference or a refused autoplay start nothing: the selected edit waits on its poster and plays through once on request. Without JavaScript the seven edits read in turn. V1.3: Podcasts is the seventh format (Max and Caleb's Lock In Podcast, Pool Talk, Jungle Talk and Food Talk), and creator ads trade Jungle Talk for a short Trezor Dare Ad excerpt. `cues` are the edit's own times (seconds) where each destination takes over, for the place line under the frame.
library.headline: One program, many formats.
library.copy: See the program move from destination films and creator ads to sponsor integrations and the moments behind the camera.
library.label: Formats

ownership._ownership: 12 Program ownership (V1.3): John's working headline, its first sentence above a waterline and its second below it (V1.2's more prominent wave and its swell, which since V1.3 flow again: each layer travels to the left at its own slow, even pace, without end and without a visible reset, the swell slower than the wave; still for reduced motion), one line on his role and three editorial chapters of his own work: shaping the campaign, directing the production and carrying it to market. No collaborators named here (the credits name them), no list of areas, no rings, no cards or pills, and nothing John did not do (no creator sourcing, legal contracts, solo filming or editing, or sole ownership of travel logistics).
ownership.headline: The experience was visible. The system behind it was not.
ownership.below: The system behind it was not.
ownership.copy: My role connected the campaign from sponsor strategy and creative direction through on-site production, distribution, and reporting.

chapters.title: Shape the campaign
chapters.text: Campaign strategy with co-sponsors, sponsor packages, creative concepts, briefs, scripts, schedules, and deliverable planning.

chapters.title: Direct the production
chapters.text: Creator coordination, shot planning, on-site direction, production scheduling, approvals, and revision guidance.

chapters.title: Carry it to market
chapters.text: Sponsor and creator liaison work, posting schedules, distribution, campaign tracking, reporting, and ongoing partner relationships.

credits._credits: 13 Credits: one system for everyone who made the work, set like a film's closing credits. The team first (V1.1): John Cowin, Maanav Porwal and Bob van der Meer, each with what they owned or collaborated on, word for word from John's brief; then the eight creators, each with their confirmed affiliations (V1.3: with the creator network gone, the credits are the one place the roster and its affiliations appear, as `people`; no handles, pictures, follower counts or categories), the co-sponsors, the brand and the hero's illustrative photography (credited here only). Since V1.2 the only place on the page that names individual collaborators. Nothing implies John edited, shot or designed the work.
credits.title: Many hands, one program.

conclusion._conclusion: 14 The conclusion: one short idea (the program kept working after each trip), then the way on to the next case study in order (Technical Product Marketing), then the shared Contact section.
conclusion.headline: The trip ends. The program keeps working.
conclusion.copy: Each activation produced an immediate body of campaign content and strengthened the creator and partner relationships behind the next opportunity. The value continued through distribution, reporting, and ongoing collaboration after everyone went home.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I turn technical complexity into a clear market narrative.
